paper: OSTI-3028840 — Intrepid MCMC: Metropolis-Hastings with Exploration (Chakroborty & Shields, CMA 2025)
notes: Five open questions grounded in the Intrepid MCMC sampler's own domain and in the specific behaviors observed during independent replication of the §4.1 nine-target benchmark. Each is genuinely unresolved by REPORT.md.

open_questions.q: How sensitive is Intrepid MCMC's efficacy to the choice of anchor point x_a when the parent density is NOT radially symmetric around x_a?
open_questions.basis: The replication used x_a=(0,0) because all nine §4.1 targets are built with a standard-Gaussian parent centered at 0, which makes the RTF reduce to the identity R(r)=r and the acceptance ratio collapse to min(1, π(x_c)/π(x_s)). REPORT.md does not test anchors offset from the parent mean, an anchor placed on a saddle, or a case with a non-symmetric parent — yet the paper's own Eqs. 21/23/26 imply that in those regimes the Γ Jacobian term and the case-specific RTF R(r) re-enter the acceptance ratio and can meaningfully change performance.
next_steps: Repeat the Gauss-Circles and Rosenbrock-Circles cases with x_a swept over a grid (e.g. (0,0), (2,0), (4,0), (0,4)) and record TVD and acceptance vs anchor location.
Construct one non-Gaussian-parent test (e.g. skew-Gumbel-Planes with anchor at the parent mode vs the parent mean) and implement the corresponding non-identity RTF explicitly.
Report a heuristic anchor-selection rule (e.g. 'anchor at posterior mean of a short pilot chain') and measure its regret vs the ideal anchor.

open_questions.q: What is the sensitivity of the reported 5×–35× TVD improvements to the RTF radial-proposal band γ ~ Uniform(a,b)?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md fixed γ ~ Uniform(0.5, 2.0) per the paper's §3.4 recommendation. That is a hidden hyperparameter: it caps a single Intrepid jump at a factor-of-2 radial rescale. On the disconnected-Circles cases the jumps must cross a mode gap of radial extent ~2×circle-radius; a narrower band could under-explore, a wider band would generate more π=0 candidates. No sensitivity sweep was attempted.
next_steps: Sweep γ band on Gauss-Circles and Rosenbrock-Circles: {(0.8,1.25), (0.5,2.0), (0.25,4.0), (0.1,10.0)} at β=0.1, 30 chains each; report TVD, acceptance, and fraction-of-π=0 candidates.
Cross-check whether narrower bands recover CMH-like failure or preserve improvement.
Investigate an adaptive γ-band that widens when acceptance is high (analogous to adaptive-MH proposal scaling).

open_questions.q: Does Intrepid's advantage persist, degrade, or invert as dimension d grows beyond 2 — specifically for the paper's own §4.2 higher-dimensional regime up to d=50?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md explicitly marks C7 as 'not attempted (scope: focused on the analytic §4.1 benchmark with exact references).' The 5×–35× gains observed are all d=2. In higher dimensions the volume of an equal-parent-probability spherical shell scales as r^{d-1}, so uniform-on-the-sphere angular proposals become exponentially sparse near any given target mode. Whether the RTF geometry still couples the proposal to π's disconnected components in d=10, 20, 50 is empirically undetermined by this replication.
next_steps: Extend intrepid.py to d∈{5, 10, 20, 50} with d-sphere angular proposals (spherical-uniform via normalized Gaussian).
Reuse a Gaussian-parent × d-dimensional Circles indicator (a small number of disjoint balls at fixed radius) and repeat the β sweep.
Compare against d-dimensional CMH and against a stratified/ensemble-MCMC baseline; report scaling of TVD-improvement factor vs d.

open_questions.q: Why does Intrepid NOT close the error-in-mean gap on Rosenbrock-Ring and Rosenbrock-Planes (both stay at ~3), while TVD DOES improve markedly on the same cases (0.66→0.08 and 0.35→0.07)?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md flags this as a partial-support for C5 and notes the paper itself acknowledges it. But the diagnosis in REPORT.md — 'the Rosenbrock mean is dominated by its heavy curved tail' — is a plausible narrative, not a measured decomposition. It is genuinely open whether the residual mean-error is (a) heavy-tail geometry that ANY finite chain would hit, (b) an Intrepid-specific under-exploration of the tail, (c) a metric artifact from the definition ||x̄ − μ_true||₂ / √(tr Σ_true) with a very large tr Σ_true, or (d) a bias from the 3M IID reference undersampling the tail.
next_steps: Decompose the mean-error contribution by radial shell: split samples into r<r_med and r≥r_med and report each shell's contribution to ||x̄ − μ_true||.
Re-run Rosenbrock-Ring with a 10M-sample IID reference to bound reference-side bias.
Extend chains to 10^6 samples (10× longer) and see whether error-in-mean drifts down for Intrepid (heavy-tail geometry) or stays flat (Intrepid-specific under-exploration).
Cross-validate with a mode-agnostic diagnostic (e.g. quantile error at 0.99) that is less tail-dominated than the raw mean.

open_questions.q: How does Intrepid MCMC compare against modern gradient-free multimodal samplers (Parallel Tempering with adaptive temperature ladder, Ensemble/affine-invariant samplers a la emcee, sequential Monte Carlo, or normalizing-flow-augmented MH) on the same nine §4.1 targets?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md compares Intrepid to CMH only. That is the paper's own headline comparison, but CMH is a very weak baseline for known-multimodal problems — the field has adopted PT/SMC/ensemble methods precisely because vanilla MH fails on disconnected modes. The 34.6× TVD improvement on Rosenbrock-Circles is real, but its POSITION within the broader landscape of methods that already handle multimodality is not established. This is central to the paper's practical claim that Intrepid is a useful drop-in.
next_steps: Implement three baselines on the §4.1 nine-target benchmark at matched wall-clock: (i) PT with 8 geometric temperatures, (ii) emcee affine-invariant with 32 walkers, (iii) SMC with 32 particles and adaptive resampling.
Report TVD, error-in-mean, acceptance, and effective-samples-per-second for each vs Intrepid(β=0.1).
Characterize the regime where Intrepid dominates (likely: cheap-to-evaluate π, low d, unknown mode locations) and where PT/SMC dominate (likely: expensive π, tempering ladder cheap).
